\chapter{Introduction}
\label{ch:intro}


This paper consolidates three sources from the Chatman Equation thesis
series -- \texttt{docs/thesis/00\_foundations.tex}, \texttt{docs/thesis/01\_admission\_algebra.tex},
and \texttt{docs/thesis/02\_receipt\_cryptography.tex} -- into a single paper,
\emph{The Admission Substrate: Refusal, Algebra, and Receipts}. It is a
clean-room rewrite driven by the machine-extracted requirements outlines for
each source and by the corpus's own formal statements
(\texttt{docs/thesis/rdf/00\_foundations.ttl},
\texttt{docs/thesis/rdf/01\_admission\_algebra.ttl},
\texttt{docs/thesis/rdf/02\_receipt\_cryptography.ttl}), not a merge of the
three papers' prose. Every definition, proposition, theorem, corollary,
axiom, and construction stated below is quoted from the corresponding
\texttt{math:statement} literal in one of those three files, identified by
its original \verb|\label{}| key so cross-references keep working; the
surrounding exposition is new.


The three sources describe themselves, in their own front matter, as
three of four pillar papers deepening one shared floor
(\texttt{00\_foundations.tex}). Their own overlap is therefore not an
editorial accident to be smoothed over silently -- it is documented, and this
consolidation follows the sources' own division of labor: \S\ref{sec:chatman-rice}
keeps only the shared floor (the five-object equation and the Rice
quarantine) from \texttt{00\_foundations}; Chapter~\ref{ch:algebra} lets
\texttt{01\_admission\_algebra} own the full denial-monoid and taxonomy
development; Chapter~\ref{ch:crypto} lets \texttt{02\_receipt\_cryptography}
own the full cryptographic chain development. \texttt{00\_foundations}'s own
admission-algebra chapter and its receipt-chain material are represented
here as minimal statements for two different reasons: the manufacturing-
morphism material (Chapter~\ref{ch:brce}) is deliberately thin because
Chapter~\ref{ch:crypto} states the full cryptographic construction it
motivates, while the lifecycle typestate category (Chapter~\ref{ch:lifecycle})
is stated here in full because neither Chapter~\ref{ch:algebra} nor
Chapter~\ref{ch:crypto} develops it further -- it is
Chapter~\ref{sec:conservation} that later builds on its typestate theorem

Every paragraph in this paper carries a \texttt{doc:register} value of

\section{Reading order}
\label{sec:readingorder}


Chapter~\ref{sec:chatman-rice} states the five-object Chatman equation
and the Rice-quarantine argument that motivates admission as a syntactic
retraction rather than a semantic decision. Chapter~\ref{ch:algebra}
develops the admission algebra in full: the denial monoid, obligations and

Chapter~\ref{ch:signed} covers signed receipts, content addressing, and

\chapter{The Chatman Equation and the Rice Quarantine}
\label{sec:chatman-rice}

\section{Five objects}
\label{sec:fiveobjects}


The project's foundational equation factors a single earlier law,
$\Act=\muop(\Obs)$, into an admission step and a manufacturing step:
$\Act=\muop(\Adm)$ with $\Adm=\im(\adm)$. Factoring the projection this way
is what makes admission a first-class, separately statable object rather
than a property folded silently into $\muop$.


\begin{definition}[The Chatman equation]\label{def:five}
The Chatman equation relates five objects: the observation space $\Obs$,
the admitted space $\Adm$, the manufacturing morphism $\muop$, the
artifact/action space $\Act$, and the receipt space $\Rec$.
\end{definition}
Source: \texttt{docs/thesis/00\_foundations.tex}, \verb|\label{def:five}|;
Lean status \texttt{verified} in both the bare-core and Mathlib lanes
(\texttt{tools/paper-factory/lean-pilot/formalization\_receipts.jsonl},
\texttt{tools/paper-factory/lean-lake/mathlib\_migration\_receipts.jsonl}).
The remaining chapters of this paper are organized around this equation's
five objects in turn: $\adm$ (Chapter~\ref{ch:algebra}), the lifecycle
category the admitted/actuated/receipted stages form
(Chapter~\ref{ch:lifecycle}), $\muop$ (Chapter~\ref{ch:brce}), and $\Rec$
(Chapters~\ref{ch:crypto}--\ref{ch:ledger}).

\section{The Rice quarantine}
\label{sec:ricequarantine}


Admission cannot be a semantic decision procedure, because the space it
decides over is, by construction, semantically opaque at the point of
admission. This is not a design choice to be relaxed by writing a smarter
admission function; it is a consequence of Rice's theorem.


\begin{axiom}[Observation space]\label{ax:obs}
There is a set $\Obs$, the observation space, whose elements are arbitrary
finite records; $\Obs$ carries no decidable semantics.
\end{axiom}
Source: \texttt{00\_foundations.tex}, \verb|\label{ax:obs}|; in praxis this
is the raw JSON payload handed to \texttt{law judge} prior to any
obligation being checked. Lean status: \texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}.


\begin{theorem}[Rice, specialized to observations]\label{thm:rice}
Rice's theorem, specialized to observations: for any non-trivial semantic
property $P$ of the function an observation denotes, the set
$\{o\in\Obs : P(o)\}$ is undecidable.
\end{theorem}
Lean status: \texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}; the bare-core proof's
first step is flagged \texttt{UNRESOLVED} in \texttt{rdf/00\_foundations.ttl}
because it rests on the external citation to Rice (1953) rather than an
in-paper statement -- the dependency is on the theorem itself, not on a
gap in the formalization.


\begin{corollary}[No semantic admission]\label{cor:noadmit}
There is no algorithm that admits an observation by deciding a non-trivial
semantic property of what it denotes; any total admission procedure
decides a syntactic, decidable surrogate instead.
\end{corollary}
Lean status: \texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}. This corollary is the
reason Chapter~\ref{ch:algebra}'s admission map $\adm$ is defined as a
retraction onto a decidable sub-language via a finite battery of total
obligations, rather than as a classifier over meaning: \texttt{cor:noadmit}
rules the latter out in principle, not just in the current implementation.

\chapter{Admission Algebra: Obligations, Denial, and Taxonomy}
\label{ch:algebra}


This chapter is where \texttt{01\_admission\_algebra.tex} owns the full
denial-monoid and taxonomy development that \texttt{00\_foundations.tex}
only sketches; per that source's own division of labor, this chapter states
the complete algebra and \S\ref{sec:fiveobjects}/\S\ref{sec:ricequarantine}
above do not restate it.

\section{Refusal as data and the admission retraction}
\label{sec:refusaldata}


Refusal is treated as an algebraic object, not a side effect: an
admission map that can fail is total once its codomain includes a tagged
refusal value paired with a machine-checkable reason.


\begin{axiom}[Refusal is data]\label{ax:refusal}
There is a distinguished refusal value $\Rfsl$ and a space of reasons
$\mathcal{R}_{\!f}$; a refusal is not the absence of an output but the pair
$(\Rfsl,r)$ with $r\in\mathcal{R}_{\!f}$ a machine-checkable reason, so
admission is total as a map into $\Adm\cup(\{\Rfsl\}\times\mathcal{R}_{\!f})$.
\end{axiom}
Source: \texttt{01\_admission\_algebra.tex}, \verb|\label{ax:refusal}|;
Lean status \texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}. In praxis this is realized
concretely by \texttt{Andon::Halted\{unmet, refusals, at\}}
(\texttt{crates/praxis-core/src/default\_law.rs}), which carries the unmet
obligation list and a timestamp rather than raising an exception; this
concrete realization is not itself Lean-formalized, only the abstract axiom
is.


\begin{definition}[Admission map]\label{def:adm}
Fix a decidable sub-collection $\Adm\subseteq\Obs$ and a finite battery of
total, computable obligations $g_1,\dots,g_m$; the admission map $\adm$ is
the partial retraction sending $o$ to $\rho(o)\in\Adm$ if all $g_i(o)=1$,
else to $\Rfsl$.
\end{definition}
\begin{proposition}[Retraction]\label{prop:retract}
$\adm$ restricted to $\Adm$ is the identity, and $\adm\circ\adm=\adm$ as
partial maps; hence $\Adm$ is a retract of $\dom(\adm)$.
\end{proposition}
Source: \texttt{00\_foundations.tex}; both \texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}.
Chapter~\ref{sec:chatman-rice}'s Rice quarantine (\texttt{cor:noadmit}) is
exactly why $g_1,\dots,g_m$ must be syntactic and decidable rather than a
semantic classifier.

\section{The denial word algebra}
\label{sec:denialalgebra}


Rather than admit-or-refuse as a bare boolean, praxis records
\emph{which} obligations failed, as a word in a fixed number of lanes. The
word space is a semilattice for a structural reason: failing more checks
can only add lanes, never remove one that already fired.


\begin{definition}[Abstract denial word]\label{def:denialabstract}
Fix $n\in\mathbb{N}$ lanes; the abstract denial word space is
$\Deny_n=\{0,1\}^{n}$ with componentwise disjunction $\lor$ and the all-zero
word $\bm 0$; lane $i$ is set in $d$ when $d_i=1$, $\supp d=\{i:d_i=1\}$,
and $d\preceq d'$ means $\forall i\,(d_i\le d_i')$.
\end{definition}
\begin{proposition}[Denial monoid]\label{prop:monoid}
$(\Deny_n,\lor,\bm 0)$ is a commutative monoid in which every element is
idempotent; it is the join-semilattice of the Boolean lattice
$(2^{[n]},\subseteq)$ under $d\mapsto\supp d$, with $\bm 0$ least and
$\bm 1$ greatest, so $d\lor d'$ is the least upper bound and $\preceq$ is
exactly $d\preceq d'\iff d\lor d'=d'$.
\end{proposition}
Source: \texttt{01\_admission\_algebra.tex}; both \texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}.
\texttt{00\_foundations.tex} states the same fact concretely as
\texttt{con:denial}/\texttt{prop:semilattice} (also both
\texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}): the total denial of an observation is
$d(o)=\bigvee_i d_i(o)$ and $\adm(o)\ne\Rfsl\iff d(o)=\bm 0$; adding
obligations can only enlarge denial, never shrink it.


\begin{definition}[Concrete denial word]\label{def:denialcode}
In praxis the denial word is \code{DenialPolarity}, a \code{repr(transparent)}
newtype over \code{u64} carved into eight byte-lanes; the clean word is
$\Adml=$ \code{DenialPolarity(0)}; seven named nonzero constants each occupy
one distinct byte lane; the product is
\code{compose(a,b)=DenialPolarity(a.0\,|\,b.0)}, bitwise OR; the admission
predicate is \code{is\_admitted(d)}$\iff d.0=0$.
\end{definition}
\begin{proposition}[Concrete word is the same semilattice]\label{prop:code_is_sl}
$\Deny=(\{\text{\code{DenialPolarity}}\},\text{compose},\Adml)$ is a bounded
commutative idempotent monoid, \code{is\_admitted} is exactly the predicate
``is the bottom element,'' and the submonoid $\langle L\rangle$ generated by
the seven named nonzero constants together with $\Adml$ is isomorphic to
$\Deny_7$ via ``which named lanes are nonzero.''
\end{proposition}
Source: \texttt{01\_admission\_algebra.tex}; both \texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}.
\code{DenialPolarity} itself is defined in the external \code{bcinr\_powl\_receipt::denial}
crate and imported by \texttt{crates/praxis-core/src/refusal.rs}, which
implements \code{compose\_denials} as the fold of this monoid over a slice
of scenarios.

\section{The fired-mask projection}
\label{sec:firedmask}


\begin{definition}[Fired-mask projection]\label{def:fired}
$\firedmap:\Deny\to\{0,1\}^{8}$ sends a word $d$ to the bit vector whose
bit $j$ equals the nonzero-indicator of byte lane $j$ of $d$:
$\firedmap(d)_j=\mathbf 1[(d.0\gg 8j)\ \&\ \text{0xFF}\ne 0]$, computed
branchlessly via $\mathbf 1[x\ne 0]=(x\mathbin{|}(-x))\gg 63$ on each lane.
\end{definition}
\begin{theorem}[Fired-mask is a monoid homomorphism]\label{thm:firedhom}
$\firedmap$ is a homomorphism of bounded commutative idempotent monoids:
$\firedmap(\Adml)=\bm 0$ and
$\firedmap(\text{compose}(a,b))=\firedmap(a)\lor\firedmap(b)$ for all
$a,b\in\Deny$; restricted to $\langle L\rangle$ it is a monoid isomorphism
onto the seven-bit image $\{0\}\times\{0,1\}^{7}$.
\end{theorem}
Source: \texttt{01\_admission\_algebra.tex}; both \texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}.
This is the projection that lets a fleet-wide admission sweep
(\S\ref{sec:pipelines}) be computed as one \code{OR} over 8-bit summaries
instead of re-inspecting every 64-bit word.

\section{Obligations and monotonicity}
\label{sec:obligations}


\begin{definition}[Obligation and its lane map]\label{def:ob}
An obligation is a first-class, hashable value the payload must satisfy
before admission; the \code{Obligation} enum has exactly three kinds; each
obligation $g$ induces a lane map $\delta_g:\Obs\to\Deny$ returning $\Adml$
if $g$ is satisfied by $o$, else $\ell(g)$; for a set $G$ the total denial
is $d_G(o)=\bigvee_{i=1}^{m}\delta_{g_i}(o)$.
\end{definition}
Source: \texttt{01\_admission\_algebra.tex}; Lean status
\texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}. The three kinds --
\code{Precondition}, \code{BlockingConstraint}, \code{EvidenceRequired} --
are enumerated in \texttt{crates/praxis-core/src/law.rs}.


\begin{proposition}[Bottom characterizes admission]\label{prop:bottom}
$\adm_G(o)\ne\Rfsl\iff d_G(o)=\Adml\iff$ every $g_i\in G$ is satisfied by
$o$.
\end{proposition}
Lean status: \texttt{verified} in the Mathlib lane
(\texttt{tools/paper-factory/lean-lake/mathlib\_migration\_receipts.jsonl}),
\texttt{unformalized} in the bare-core lane after three attempts
(\texttt{tools/paper-factory/lean-pilot/formalization\_receipts.jsonl}
records the blocker as a Lean~4.31 API mismatch on
\code{List.mem\_cons\_self} in the induction step of
\code{foldl\_compose\_eq\_Adml\_iff}, with the three supporting lemmas
already verified in the same run). This paper does not claim dual-lane
verification for \texttt{prop:bottom}: cite the Mathlib result only.


\begin{theorem}[Admission is antitone]\label{thm:mono}
Let $G\subseteq G'$ be obligation sets; then $d_G(o)\preceq d_{G'}(o)$ for
every observation $o$, hence $\Adm_{G'}\subseteq\Adm_G$: adding obligations
can only enlarge denial and shrink admission, never admit an observation a
smaller obligation set refused.
\end{theorem}
\begin{corollary}[Galois monotonicity]\label{cor:galois}
The assignment $G\mapsto\Adm_G$ is an order-reversing map from
$(2^{\mathcal{G}},\subseteq)$ to $(2^{\Obs},\subseteq)$:
$G\subseteq G'\Rightarrow\Adm_{G'}\subseteq\Adm_G$; the empty obligation
set admits everything ($\Adm_\varnothing=\Obs$), and enlarging obligations
monotonically tightens the gate.
\end{corollary}
Lean status: both \texttt{verified} in the Mathlib lane, \texttt{blocked}
(never attempted) in the bare-core lane.


\begin{proposition}[Obligation classification is total]\label{prop:obtotal}
The map $\scnop:\text{Obligation}\to\Scnset$ implemented by
\code{From<\&Obligation> for RefusalScenario} is a total function realized
by a wildcard-free match over the three \code{Obligation} kinds; because
the match has no wildcard arm, totality is a static property of the
program, not a runtime hope.
\end{proposition}
Lean status: \texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}.

\section{The refusal taxonomy}
\label{sec:taxonomy}


\begin{definition}[Refusal taxonomy]\label{def:tax}
The category set $\Catset$ is the eight-element enum
Identity/Capacity/Topology/Temporal/Lifecycle/Authorization/Prerequisites/Reserved;
the scenario set $\Scnset$ is the thirteen-variant \code{RefusalScenario}
enum partitioned into three obligation-driven, seven denial-lane, and three
logic/andon variants; the category map $\catop:\Scnset\to\Catset$ is
\code{RefusalScenario::category}.
\end{definition}
Source: \texttt{01\_admission\_algebra.tex}, \verb|\label{def:tax}|; Lean
status \texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}. \texttt{00\_foundations.tex}
states the same set-up abstractly as \texttt{def:taxonomy}
(a pair $(S,\mathrm{cat})$, $\mathrm{cat}:S\to C$ total onto the
eight-element $C$) and \texttt{prop:total} (totality plus the lane map's
single-lane inverse being a section over the seven named lanes), both
also \texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}; that abstract pair and this
concrete enum are the same object under the correspondence
$C\leftrightarrow\Catset$, $S\leftrightarrow\Scnset$. A caveat on the
\texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified} status: the Lean formalizations behind
it (\texttt{tools/paper-factory/lean-pilot/def\_tax.lean},
\texttt{tools/paper-factory/lean-lake/Praxis/Corpus/def\_tax.lean}) do not
use the real \code{RefusalScenario} variant names from
\texttt{crates/praxis-core/src/refusal.rs:82--136} (\code{BlockingConstraint},
\code{MissingEvidence}, \code{UnsatisfiedPrecondition},
\code{WatchdogDrained}, \code{PreconditionFailed}, \code{SlaBreach},
\code{AuthorizationDenied}, \code{ResourceExhausted},
\code{ObjectLifecycleViolation}, \code{ConformanceGateFailed},
\code{KernelDenied}, \code{KernelInvalid}, \code{AndonInvariantViolated});
both lanes instead formalize an invented placeholder enum
(\S\ref{sec:taxonomy-disputed} names both). The \texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}
status therefore certifies that a placeholder thirteen-variant enum's
category map is total and shaped like \texttt{def:tax}'s statement, not
that the thirteen real variants each land in the category asserted by the
real \code{RefusalScenario::category} match at \texttt{refusal.rs:142--158}.

\section{Taxonomy totality: a disputed claim (speculative)}
\label{sec:taxonomy-disputed}


\begin{disputed}[Totality and Reserved's preimage]\label{thm:total}
The category map $\catop:\Scnset\to\Catset$ is total (every one of the
thirteen scenarios has exactly one category), mechanized (compiler-certified
via a wildcard-free match), and its image is $\Catset\setminus\{\text{Reserved}\}$:
exactly seven buckets are inhabited, and Reserved has empty preimage.
\end{disputed}
This claim is marked \emph{disputed}, not evidence-bound, but the dispute is
narrower than the two Lean receipts alone suggest, and needs to be stated
precisely: \textbf{neither Lean lane formalizes this claim against the
real \code{RefusalScenario} enum} quoted in \S\ref{sec:taxonomy}
(\code{BlockingConstraint}, \code{MissingEvidence},
\code{UnsatisfiedPrecondition}, \code{WatchdogDrained},
\code{PreconditionFailed}, \code{SlaBreach}, \code{AuthorizationDenied},
\code{ResourceExhausted}, \code{ObjectLifecycleViolation},
\code{ConformanceGateFailed}, \code{KernelDenied}, \code{KernelInvalid},
\code{AndonInvariantViolated}; \texttt{crates/praxis-core/src/refusal.rs:82--136}).
Both lanes instead formalize an invented placeholder enum.
\texttt{tools/paper-factory/lean-lake/Praxis/Corpus/def\_tax.lean} names its
thirteen variants \code{schemaViolation}, \code{policyViolation},
\code{temporalViolation}, \code{lane1Denial}--\code{lane7Denial},
\code{logicContradiction}, \code{andonPull}, \code{andonEscalation}, and
hard-codes the last three to \code{Category.Reserved} by fiat.
\texttt{tools/paper-factory/lean-pilot/def\_tax.lean} names its thirteen
variants \code{schemaObligation}, \code{policyObligation},
\code{signatureObligation}, \code{denialA}--\code{denialG},
\code{logicAndon1}--\code{logicAndon3}, and likewise hard-codes the last
three (\code{logicAndon1}/\code{2}/\code{3}) to \code{Reserved}. Neither
set of invented names, and neither hard-coded mapping, corresponds to any
arm of the real \code{RefusalScenario::category} match
(\texttt{refusal.rs:142--158}), which never returns \code{Reserved} for any
of its thirteen real arms: Reserved's preimage in the actual shipped code
is genuinely empty, exactly as the original source proof
(\texttt{docs/thesis/01\_admission\_algebra.tex:380--446}) states using the
real variant names and an explicit per-variant table.
\par
Given that, the two Lean receipts describe two different placeholder
enums, not the real one. The bare-core lane's \texttt{thm\_total.lean}
reports \code{thm:total} \texttt{verified} after three attempts
(\texttt{tools/paper-factory/lean-pilot/formalization\_receipts.jsonl}),
but its own file comment records that it does so only by dropping the
Reserved-exclusion clause and proving the opposite instead -- that its
placeholder \code{catop} is surjective onto \emph{all eight} categories,
\code{Reserved} included: ``the source LaTeX additionally claims the
image excludes \code{Reserved}... That does not hold for the actual
verified \code{catop} in \code{def\_tax.lean}... This file formalizes the
part that is true of the real definition.'' So the bare-core
\texttt{verified} status is \emph{not} a verification of the
Reserved-empty-preimage clause quoted above; it verifies a different,
weaker theorem about its own placeholder enum. The Mathlib-lane
re-derivation
(\texttt{tools/paper-factory/lean-lake/mathlib\_migration\_receipts.jsonl})
reports \code{thm:total} \texttt{unformalized}, with an explicit
\code{last\_error} recording that its own placeholder \texttt{def:tax}
maps \code{logicContradiction}, \code{andonPull}, and
\code{andonEscalation} into \code{Category.Reserved} -- again, a fact
about the placeholder enum that lane invented, not about
\code{RefusalScenario}.
\par
The dispute this paper reports is therefore a dispute between two
mutually inconsistent Lean placeholder formalizations of \texttt{def:tax},
not a demonstrated property -- verified, refuted, or otherwise -- of the
\code{RefusalScenario} taxonomy actually shipped in this repository.
Whether \texttt{thm:total}, quoted above with its real variant names,
holds of the real code is not established by either Lean lane; reading
the real \code{category()} match directly (\texttt{refusal.rs:142--158})
does exhibit the property the theorem claims (seven inhabited buckets,
Reserved empty, matching \texttt{01\_admission\_algebra.tex}'s own
proof), but that is a manual proof-by-inspection of the source, not a
Lean-checked one. This paper therefore reports both lane outcomes side by
side and does not present either the totality/coverage half of
\texttt{thm:total} or its refutation as machine-verified fact about the
real taxonomy; \S\ref{sec:taxonomy} above cites only \texttt{def:tax} and
\texttt{00\_foundations}'s \texttt{prop:total}, neither of which makes the
disputed Reserved-preimage claim.

\section{Partiality at the lane-decoder boundary}
\label{sec:decoder}


\begin{definition}[Lane decoder]\label{def:decoder}
Let $L=\{\Adml,c_1,\dots,c_7\}\subseteq\Deny$ be the clean word together
with the seven named single-lane constants; the lane decoder
$\scnop_\ell:\Deny\rightharpoonup\Scnset$ is
\code{scenario\_for\_denial\_lane}: it returns \code{None} on $\Adml$,
returns the matching denial-lane scenario on each $c_i$, and returns
\code{None} on every word not in $L$.
\end{definition}
\begin{proposition}[Partiality is inherent]\label{prop:partial}
$\scnop_\ell$ is a partial map, definite (as \code{Some}) only on
$L\setminus\{\Adml\}$; it is not realizable as a wildcard-free exhaustive
match because its domain $\Deny$ is an open value space of cardinality
$2^{64}$, not a closed enum, so exhaustiveness over the seven single lanes
is a runtime test obligation, not a static type obligation.
\end{proposition}
Source: \texttt{01\_admission\_algebra.tex}; both \texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}.
The point of stating this alongside \texttt{prop:obtotal} (which \emph{is}
total) is that the taxonomy has two boundaries with different totality
character: classification of a closed \code{Obligation} enum is a static
guarantee, decoding an open 64-bit word is not.

\section{Assembled totality: a disputed corollary (speculative)}
\label{sec:assembled-disputed}


\begin{speculative}[Encoder is a section]\label{prop:section}
The lane encoder $\laneop:\Scnset\to\Deny$ implemented by \code{denial\_lane}
is total via a wildcard-free match over all thirteen scenarios; restricted
to the seven denial-lane scenarios $\Scnset_\ell$, it and $\scnop_\ell$ form
a section-retraction pair, so the seven single lanes and the seven
denial-lane scenarios are in bijection; the remaining six scenarios map
onto closest-fit lanes and are not in that bijection's range.
\end{speculative}
\begin{speculative}[Assembled totality]\label{cor:assembled}
Composing the total maps of \texttt{prop:obtotal} and \texttt{prop:section}
with the total classification of \texttt{thm:total}: every unmet obligation
(via $\catop\circ\scnop$) and every non-$\Adml$ single denial lane (via
$\catop\circ\scnop_\ell$ on $L\setminus\{\Adml\}$) maps to exactly one of
the seven inhabited categories; no obligation failure and no fired single
lane is left unclassified.
\end{speculative}
These two statements are wrapped in the \texttt{speculative} environment,
not \texttt{proposition}/\texttt{corollary}, because \texttt{cor:assembled}
is disputed for the same reason \S\ref{sec:taxonomy-disputed} is: it is
quoted verbatim from \texttt{rdf/01\_admission\_algebra.ttl}'s
\texttt{math:cor\_assembled}, whose own \texttt{math:dependsOn} names
\texttt{math:thm\_total}, not \texttt{def:tax}, and so inherits
\S\ref{sec:taxonomy-disputed}'s dispute rather than standing apart from
it. The ``seven inhabited categories'' conclusion restated here depends on
the Reserved-exclusion half of \texttt{thm:total}, which
\S\ref{sec:taxonomy-disputed} shows is not established -- by either Lean
lane -- against the real \code{RefusalScenario} enum: both lanes' Lean
receipts describe invented placeholder enums with different variant
names, not \code{RefusalScenario} itself, so neither lane's outcome for
\texttt{prop:section}/\texttt{cor:assembled} bears directly on the real
taxonomy. Lean status: \texttt{prop:section} and \texttt{cor:assembled}
are both \texttt{verified} in the bare-core lane (against that lane's
placeholder enum); in the Mathlib lane both are \texttt{blocked} (not
attempted, not failed in their own right) -- that blocking follows
\texttt{thm:total}'s own Mathlib status being
\texttt{unformalized}/contradicted, not from independent difficulty. This
paper does not present \texttt{cor:assembled}'s conclusion as
machine-verified fact about the real taxonomy, only about the bare-core
lane's placeholder formalization of it.

\section{Pipelines and fleet-wide denial}
\label{sec:pipelines}


\begin{definition}[Pipeline denial]\label{def:pipeline}
Let \code{Stage} be the set of admission stages; fix $o$ and let
$\varphi_o:\text{Stage}\to\Deny$ send a stage to the denial word it emits
on $o$; a pipeline is a finite sequence $w=s_1\cdots s_k\in\text{Stage}^{*}$,
an element of the free monoid on \code{Stage}; its aggregate denial is
$\Phi_o(w)=\bigvee_{i=1}^{k}\varphi_o(s_i)$, $\Phi_o(\varepsilon)=\Adml$.
\end{definition}
\begin{theorem}[Aggregate denial is the free homomorphism]\label{thm:freehom}
$\Phi_o:(\text{Stage}^{*},\cdot,\varepsilon)\to(\Deny,\text{compose},\Adml)$
is the unique monoid homomorphism extending $\varphi_o$ along
$\text{Stage}\hookrightarrow\text{Stage}^{*}$; because the target is
commutative and idempotent, $\Phi_o(w)$ depends only on the set of distinct
stage-denials occurring in $w$, invariant under reordering and repetition.
\end{theorem}
Source: \texttt{01\_admission\_algebra.tex}; this is a different
\texttt{def:pipeline} from the validator pipeline of
\S\ref{sec:validatorpipeline} -- same label, two constructions in the two
source papers, disambiguated here by chapter. Both statements above are
\texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}.


\begin{corollary}[All-stages admission]\label{cor:allstages}
$\Phi_o(w)=\Adml\iff\varphi_o(s_i)=\Adml$ for every stage $s_i$ in $w$; a
single refusing stage refuses the whole pipeline, and the aggregate word
records every lane that fired anywhere along $w$.
\end{corollary}
Lean status: \texttt{verified} in the Mathlib lane; the bare-core lane
reports \texttt{unformalized} after three attempts, blocked on a
\code{funext}/\code{congrFun} plumbing bug whose root cause the receipt
records as already understood but not re-verified within the attempt
budget.


\begin{proposition}[Fleet sweep]\label{prop:fleet}
Let a fleet of $N$ manufactures produce aggregate words
$\Phi^{(1)},\dots,\Phi^{(N)}$, packed as
$b^{(r)}=\firedmap(\Phi^{(r)})\in\{0,1\}^{8}$; then
$\firedmap(\Phi_o(w))=\bigvee_i\firedmap(\varphi_o(s_i))$, and a fleet
admission sweep is one linear pass computing $\bigvee_r b^{(r)}$, returning
$\bm 0$ iff every agent is admitted.
\end{proposition}
Lean status: \texttt{verified} in the Mathlib lane, \texttt{blocked} (not
attempted) in the bare-core lane.

\section{Logical quarantine and proof-carrying admission}
\label{sec:logicquarantine}


The same Rice-quarantine discipline that bounds obligation admission
(\S\ref{sec:ricequarantine}) also bounds admission of logic queries: a
query is admitted only if it lies inside a fixed, decidable Horn fragment,
never by attempting to decide an unbounded logic program's semantics.


\begin{definition}[Bounded Horn admission]\label{def:logicadm}
\code{prolog8} admits a query, fact block, or rule only if it lies in a
bounded, decidable Horn fragment: arity $\le 8$, rule body $\le 8$ atoms,
$\le 8$ variables, proof fan-in $\le 8$; no cut, no dynamic mutation,
stratified negation, bounded recursion, no runtime text parsing, no side
effects, interned terms; violations are enumerated by \code{RejectionCode}.
\end{definition}
Lean status: \texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}.


\begin{definition}[Query result]\label{def:queryresult}
\code{Kernel::query} returns \code{QueryResult}, one of
\code{Answered(Vec<Decision>)}, \code{Denied(Box<Decision>)}, or
\code{Invalid(RejectionCode)}; a \code{Decision} carries a proof (a
\code{Vec<ProofNode>} DAG, positive or negative) and a receipt sufficient
for deterministic replay.
\end{definition}
\begin{theorem}[Trichotomy]\label{thm:trichotomy}
For a query $q$ evaluated against an admitted kernel, exactly one of
Answered (a positive proof DAG with fan-in $\le 8$ plus receipt), Denied
(a negative proof plus receipt), or Invalid (a \code{RejectionCode}, no
proof) holds.
\end{theorem}
Lean status: both \texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}.


\begin{proposition}[Bounded certificate]\label{prop:boundedcert}
Every proof node emitted by the kernel has fan-in $\le 8$ and every rule
body has $\le 8$ atoms, so a proof is a bounded-degree DAG; its rolling
\code{proof\_root} is a single fixed-width hash field of the receipt, and a
bounded-context verifier checks a query outcome in $O(\CL)$ by recomputing
\code{proof\_root}.
\end{proposition}
Lean status: \texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}.


\begin{proposition}[Logical refusal embeds into the denial monoid]\label{prop:embed}
The refusing branches of \texttt{thm:trichotomy} embed into
$(\Deny,\text{compose},\Adml)$ via the taxonomy: \code{run\_kernel\_query}
maps Denied to scenario \code{KernelDenied} (category Authorization) and
Invalid to \code{KernelInvalid} (category Identity); by \code{denial\_lane}
both compose into lane \code{CONFORMANCE\_GATE\_FAILED}, so a logical
refusal is subject to monotonicity, classification, pipeline composition,
and fired-mask projection exactly as any obligation refusal.
\end{proposition}
Lean status: \texttt{verified} in the bare-core lane, \texttt{blocked}
(not attempted) in the Mathlib lane. This is the proposition that unifies
\S\ref{sec:logicquarantine} with the rest of this chapter: logic-engine
outcomes are not a second, separate refusal system.

\section{The untrusted-observation boundary}
\label{sec:obsauth}


Admission algebra so far treats $\Obs$ as given. When observations arrive
from another agent rather than from the environment directly, a further
question arises: which observations may an admitted actor treat as
authoritative for its own admission?


\begin{definition}[Observation authority]\label{def:obsauth}
Let $\Obs$ be the raw observation space; an observation $o\in\Obs$ is
authoritative ($o\in\Obs^{*}$) if it was produced by an admitted actuation
with a chained receipt; all other observations are untrusted; the
proposer's admission map $\adm_{\mathrm{prop}}$ retracts $\Obs$ onto
$\Adm_{\mathrm{prop}}$ by treating every inbound observation as untrusted
until its receipt chain satisfies the obligation battery $G_{\mathrm{prop}}$.
\end{definition}
\begin{proposition}[Boundary is enforced]\label{prop:boundary}
Under \texttt{def:obsauth}, \code{praxis-proposer} enforces
$\im\muop_{\mathrm{prop}}\subseteq\Adm_{\mathrm{prop}}$: no proposal is
manufactured from an unadmitted observation; the generic
\code{engine::Proposer<D: Domain>} restricts enumeration to
\code{Domain::lawful\_targets}, the per-entity evidence gate, and emits
every candidate as an untrusted observation ($\Obs$, not $\Obs^{*}$) that
must independently pass Rice quarantine and admission -- realized by
\code{praxis-core}'s \code{Obligation} enum and \code{Admit} trait
(\texttt{crates/praxis-core/src/law.rs}) -- before it has effect;
\code{praxis-proposer} itself contains no \code{Obligation} battery and
never calls \code{Admit::admit}.
\end{proposition}
Source: \texttt{01\_admission\_algebra.tex}; both statements
\texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}, realized in
\texttt{crates/praxis-proposer}. This boundary is what makes an untrusted
proposer's claim about its own admissibility non-self-certifying: only a
chained receipt (Chapter~\ref{ch:crypto}) counts as evidence of prior
admission, never the proposer's own assertion.

\chapter{Lifecycle as a Typestate Category}
\label{ch:lifecycle}


This material is unique to \texttt{00\_foundations.tex}: neither
\texttt{01\_admission\_algebra} nor \texttt{02\_receipt\_cryptography}
claims it, so it is stated here in full rather than as a cross-reference.


\begin{definition}[Lifecycle category]\label{def:lifecat}
$\Life$ is the free category on the linear quiver
$\Raw\xrightarrow{j}\Val\xrightarrow{a}\Admd\xrightarrow{r}\Rcpt$, with four
objects and three generating arrows judge, admit, receipt.
\end{definition}
\begin{proposition}[Hom-sets are singletons or empty]\label{prop:hom}
For stages $X,Y$ of $\Life$, the hom-set $\Life(X,Y)$ has exactly one
element if $Y$ is reachable from $X$ along the quiver, and is empty
otherwise.
\end{proposition}
Source: \texttt{00\_foundations.tex}; both \texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}.
No backward or skipping morphism exists in $\Life$: there is no arrow
$\Admd\to\Val$ and no arrow $\Raw\to\Admd$ that bypasses $a$.


\begin{construction}[Sequential token model]\label{def:seqtoken}
The lifecycle process is modeled as a safe Petri net (3-Node SEQ POWL token
game) over the marking
$M=(\code{TOK\_START},\code{TOK\_JUDGED},\code{TOK\_ADMITTED},\code{TOK\_DONE})$,
with fitness $\Fitness\in[0,1]$ in Q16.16.
\end{construction}
Source: \texttt{00\_foundations.tex}; Lean status
\texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}. This is the same fitness quantity
Chapter~\ref{sec:validatorpipeline} defines concretely
(\texttt{def:fitness}) for the validator's \code{token\_replay} stage.


\begin{theorem}[Typestate realizes the category]\label{thm:typestate}
Interpreting each lifecycle stage as a \code{LawObject} type family, the
exposed stage-changing operations denote exactly the generating arrows of
$\Life$; every well-typed stage-changing program is a composite of $j,a,r$,
illegal transitions are uninhabited hom-sets, and no law object can be
receipted twice.
\end{theorem}
\begin{corollary}[The admissible sub-category is exactly $\Life$]\label{cor:subcat}
The sub-category of admissible morphisms a program may actually perform is
precisely $\Life$; illegal-transition-is-a-type-error is a static fact
about inhabited hom-sets, not a runtime check.
\end{corollary}
Source: \texttt{00\_foundations.tex}; both \texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}.
In praxis, \code{LawObject<Payload, S: Stage, Law>}
(\texttt{crates/praxis-core/src/law.rs}) has a sealed \code{Stage} trait
with private phantom fields: only $j$, $a$, $r$ are constructible,
backward/skip transitions do not type-check, and \code{receipt()} consumes
its receiver, so double-receipting a value is a compile error, not a
runtime check caught by \texttt{cor:subcat}.

\chapter{Manufacture and the Bounded Receipted Chatman Equation}
\label{ch:brce}


\begin{definition}[Manufacturing morphism]\label{def:mu}
A manufacturing morphism is a deterministic computable map
$\muop:\Adm\to\Act$ satisfying determinism/reproducibility (M1) and
boundedness (M2); $\muop$ is undefined off $\Adm$ and
$\muop(\Rfsl)=\Rfsl$.
\end{definition}
\begin{proposition}[Determinism gives a partial function on $\Obs$]\label{prop:mudet}
Under (M1), $x\mapsto\muop(x)$ is single-valued, so
$o\mapsto\muop(\adm(o))$ is a partial function on $\Obs$: two runs on the
same admitted input agree bit-for-bit.
\end{proposition}
Source: \texttt{00\_foundations.tex}; both \texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}.
Praxis instantiates $\muop$ concretely as PDDL8 domain/problem manufacture
from a \code{pdl:} RDF ontology (\code{mfg pddl} over \code{bcinr-pddl}),
hashed with BLAKE3 as a determinism witness; that specific instantiation
claim carries no Lean label of its own -- it is an engineering fact about
\texttt{crates/pddl-index}, cited here as evidence-bound because the crate
and command exist, not because it is machine-checked.


\begin{definition}[Chained receipt, minimal form]\label{def:receipt}
Fix a collision-resistant hash $\chainH$; the frame is
$\mathsf{fr}=\langle\theta,\chainH(b)\rangle$ and the chained receipt is
$h_{+}=\chainH(h_{-}\Vert\mathsf{fr})$; the receipt is the
$\le\CL$-chunk tuple (verdict, $h_+$, $\Fitness$, reason).
\end{definition}
\begin{definition}[Conformance fitness]\label{def:fit}
Conformance fitness $\Fitness\in[0,1]$ is one minus the fraction of tokens
a replay was forced to consume on unenabled lifecycle transitions;
$\Fitness=1$ iff the replay never attempted a disabled firing.
\end{definition}
\begin{lemma}[Chain commitment]\label{lem:commit}
Under collision resistance of $\chainH$, the chain value $h_+$ is a
binding commitment to $(h_-,\mathsf{fr})$; by induction $h_+$ binds the
entire causal prefix.
\end{lemma}
Source: \texttt{00\_foundations.tex}; all three \texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}.
This minimal, single-frame statement is deliberately thin:
Chapter~\ref{ch:crypto} is where the full byte-level frame layout, the
99-byte hash body, and the genesis-anchored chain recurrence are stated and
proved. \texttt{def:fit} is realized by \code{PowlReplayVerifier}
(\texttt{crates/praxis-core/src/replay\_adapter.rs}), computed in Q16.16
fixed point.


\begin{definition}[Bounded Receipted Chatman Equation]\label{def:brce}
A system satisfies the Bounded Receipted Chatman Equation (\BRCE) if for
every actuated artifact it maintains the admission gate (B1), bounded
manufacture (B2), receipt totality (B3), and conformance (B4).
\end{definition}
Source: \texttt{00\_foundations.tex}; Lean status
\texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}. \BRCE\ packages
\texttt{def:adm} (Chapter~\ref{ch:algebra}), \texttt{def:mu}/\texttt{prop:mudet}
above, \texttt{def:receipt}, and \texttt{def:fit} into the single invariant
that Conservation of Consequence (\S\ref{sec:conservation}) is stated
under.

\chapter{Receipt Cryptography: Frames, Chains, and the Faithful Chain Theorem}
\label{ch:crypto}


This chapter is where \texttt{02\_receipt\_cryptography.tex} owns the
byte-level frame layout and hash-chain construction that
Chapter~\ref{ch:brce} only sketches as a single-frame commitment
(\texttt{def:receipt}, \texttt{lem:commit}).

\section{Frame layout and content commitment}
\label{sec:frames}


\begin{construction}[Frame]\label{def:frame}
A frame $\fr$ is the record
$\langle\code{instruction\_id}, \code{fired\_mask}, \code{denial},
\code{obj\_refs}[0{:}8], \code{ts\_ns}, \code{activity\_idx},
\code{node\_kind}, \code{prior\_hash}\rangle$, laid out as a
\code{repr(C, align(64))} structure occupying exactly $128$ bytes, with
$5$ bytes of interior padding.
\end{construction}
\begin{definition}[Hash body]\label{def:body}
The hash body $\body(\fr)\in\{0,1\}^{8\cdot 99}$ is the $99$-byte
serialization produced by \code{to\_hash\_bytes}; it is a total, injective
function of the semantic fields of $\fr$ (all fields except the structural
\code{pad}).
\end{definition}
\begin{proposition}[Body injectivity]\label{prop:bodyinj}
$\body$ is injective on the semantic field tuple: if
$\body(\fr)=\body(\fr')$ then $\fr$ and $\fr'$ agree on every field of
Definition~\ref{def:frame}.
\end{proposition}
Source: \texttt{02\_receipt\_cryptography.tex}; all three
\texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}.


\begin{construction}[Payload commitment]\label{con:commit}
Let $p\in\{0,1\}^{*}$ be the canonical JSON bytes of an admitted payload
and $\dg(p)=\chainH(p)\in\{0,1\}^{256}$ its digest; partition $\dg(p)$ into
eight $32$-bit little-endian words $w_0,\dots,w_7$ and set
$\code{obj\_refs}[i]=\code{PackedObjRef}(w_i)$ via the raw tuple
constructor, preserving all $32$ bits.
\end{construction}
\begin{proposition}[Content, not a handle, is committed]\label{prop:payloadcommit}
Under Construction~\ref{con:commit}, $\body(\fr)$ determines $\dg(p)$, and
by Proposition~\ref{prop:bodyinj} any change to $\dg(p)$ changes
$\body(\fr)$: a frame commits to the content of the artifact, not an
opaque handle.
\end{proposition}
Source: \texttt{02\_receipt\_cryptography.tex}; \texttt{con:commit} is
\texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}. \texttt{prop:payloadcommit} is
\texttt{blocked} in the bare-core lane but \texttt{verified} in the
Mathlib lane -- the two lanes disagree by status, not by content; cite
the Mathlib result only.

\section{Hash chain construction and determinism}
\label{sec:chain}


\begin{construction}[Genesis]\label{def:genesis}
The genesis chain value is $\Genesis=\chainH(\bm 0_{32})$; a run may
additionally bind a domain seed
$\Genesis_{\mathrm{dom}}=\chainH(\text{project-version-genesis})$ so
chains from distinct projects or versions cannot cross-verify.
\end{construction}
\begin{definition}[Chain recurrence]\label{def:chain}
For a frame $\fr$ with predecessor commitment $h_{-}$, the successor
commitment is $h_{+}=\chainH(h_{-}\concat\body(\fr))$; a chain
$\Ledger=(\fr_1,\dots,\fr_n)$ has $h_0=\Genesis$ and
$h_t=\chainH(h_{t-1}\concat\body(\fr_t))$, terminal value $h_n$.
\end{definition}
Source: \texttt{02\_receipt\_cryptography.tex}; both
\texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}.


\begin{proposition}[Deterministic fold]\label{prop:fold}
$h_n$ is a deterministic function of $(\Genesis,\fr_1,\dots,\fr_n)$,
computable by a single left fold; equal inputs give bit-identical $h_n$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proposition}[No code-path drift]\label{prop:nodrift}
A receipt emitted by \code{LawObject::receipt\_with\_record} and later
recomputed by \code{ReceiptRecord::recompute\_chain\_hash} both route
through \code{build\_admission\_frame} and \code{chain\_from\_frame}; for
identical stored fields they compute identical $h_{+}$, so any
disagreement is attributable to a changed stored field, never divergent
code paths.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proposition}[Prefix commitment]\label{prop:prefix}
For each $t$, $h_t$ commits every frame $\fr_1,\dots,\fr_t$ and the
genesis value; the terminal $h_n$ commits the entire history.
\end{proposition}
Source: \texttt{02\_receipt\_cryptography.tex}; all three
\texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}. \texttt{prop:nodrift} is the reason a
recompute mismatch localizes to data, never to which function ran --
compare Theorem~\ref{thm:localize} below.

\section{The Faithful Chain Theorem}
\label{sec:faithful}


\begin{axiom}[BLAKE3 collision resistance]\label{ax:cr}
$\chainH$ (BLAKE3) is collision-resistant: no PPT adversary finds
$x\ne y$ with $\chainH(x)=\chainH(y)$ except with negligible probability
$\varepsilon(\lambda)$, $\lambda=256$, birthday bound $\sim 2^{128}$.
\end{axiom}
Source: \texttt{02\_receipt\_cryptography.tex}; Lean status
\texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}. This formalizes the assumption as an
axiom -- it is not, and does not purport to be, a proof that BLAKE3 is
collision-resistant.


\begin{theorem}[Faithful Chain Theorem]\label{thm:faithful}
Let $\Ledger=(\fr_1,\dots,\fr_n)$ have terminal commitment $h_n$, and
$\Ledger'$ differ in at least one committed field of at least one frame;
if $\Ledger'$ has the same terminal $h_n$, a collision of $\chainH$ has
been exhibited. Under Axiom~\ref{ax:cr}, altering any committed field
while preserving $h_n$ succeeds only with probability $\le\varepsilon(\lambda)$.
\end{theorem}
This theorem is not machine-verified in either lane: it does not appear in
the bare-core receipts file
(\texttt{tools/paper-factory/lean-pilot/formalization\_receipts.jsonl}),
and the Mathlib lane
(\texttt{tools/paper-factory/lean-lake/mathlib\_migration\_receipts.jsonl})
records its status as \texttt{excluded}. It is stated and cited here as
the pen-and-paper argument the source paper gives, not upgraded on the
strength of any Lean result.


\begin{corollary}[Verification cost]\label{cor:cost}
A verifier checking a single frame recomputes one fold and one equality
test: $O(1)$ time and space, independent of $n$; checking the boundary
projection of a whole run is $O(\CL)$.
\end{corollary}
Lean status: \texttt{blocked} in both lanes. The $O(\CL)$ boundary bound
additionally rests, per \texttt{rdf/02\_receipt\_cryptography.ttl}'s own
annotation, on the keystone paper's Comprehension-Verification Gap result,
which is out of scope for this consolidation -- doubly unverified here.

\chapter{Conservation of Consequence and the Validator Pipeline}
\label{sec:conservation}

\section{Conservation of Consequence}
\label{sec:conservation-thm}


\texttt{thm:conservation} is stated in both \texttt{00\_foundations.tex}
(abstractly, over $\muop$ and $\adm$) and \texttt{02\_receipt\_cryptography.tex}
(concretely, over the frame chain of \texttt{def:chain}); the two are the
same theorem at different levels of concreteness, both carrying the same
label, and both \texttt{blocked} in both Lean lanes. This paper states the
concrete form and cites the abstract form as its motivation.


\begin{theorem}[Conservation of Consequence]\label{thm:conservation}
Fix $\Act=\muop(\Adm)$ with the receipt chain of Definition~\ref{def:chain}.
Every actuated artifact is caused by an admitted $x\ne\Rfsl$; each
actuation is positioned by exactly one appended frame, with
$\Phi:\text{actuation}\mapsto h_{+}$ injective up to collision; each
committed frame is attributed at least one admitted cause via bytes
$[24,56)$ and $[16,24)$.
\end{theorem}
Abstractly (\texttt{00\_foundations.tex}): under \BRCE, the map
$a\mapsto h_+(a)$ from actuated artifacts to receipt-chain positions is
well defined and injective up to hash collision, and every actuated
artifact is the image under $\muop$ of exactly one admitted observation.
Lean status: \texttt{blocked}/\texttt{blocked} in both lanes, in both
source papers -- neither has been machine-checked; both are pen-and-paper
arguments only.


\begin{corollary}[No orphans, no double-counting]\label{cor:orphan}
No actuated artifact lacks a chain position (no orphan) and no chain
position is shared by two actuations (no double-count); consequence is
neither created without an admitted cause nor recorded without a unique
receipt slot.
\end{corollary}
Lean status: \texttt{blocked}/\texttt{blocked}. Per
\texttt{rdf/02\_receipt\_cryptography.ttl}'s own annotation, the proof step
\code{rc\_proof\_thm\_conservation\_s1} rests on Chapter~\ref{ch:lifecycle}'s
typestate theorem (\texttt{thm:typestate}/\texttt{cor:subcat}); this
chapter cites that dependency rather than re-deriving it.


\begin{corollary}[\BRCE\ antibody]\label{cor:antibody-brce}
Under \BRCE\ the overclaim set (actuations lacking a valid receipt) is
empty as an invariant: the admissible magnitude of any claim is bounded by
what the mechanism can receipt.
\end{corollary}
Source: \texttt{00\_foundations.tex}, \verb|\label{cor:antibody}|. This is
the first of the two statements this consolidation must disambiguate
under that shared label (\S\ref{ch:intro} above); the second,
distinguished here as \emph{the scope antibody corollary}, is
Corollary~\ref{cor:antibody-scope} in Chapter~\ref{sec:scope} and is a
different claim about what a \emph{verified} receipt chain does not
license asserting. Lean status: \texttt{blocked}/\texttt{blocked}.

\section{The validator pipeline}
\label{sec:validatorpipeline}


\begin{definition}[Validator pipeline]\label{def:pipeline-val}
The validator runs five stages in fixed order over a ledger
$(\fr_t)_{t=1}^{n}$ -- \code{schema}, \code{chain\_recompute},
\code{chain\_linkage}, \code{monotonic}, \code{token\_replay} -- each
returning Pass/Fail/Skip, reporting all stage outcomes rather than
short-circuiting.
\end{definition}
Source: \texttt{02\_receipt\_cryptography.tex}, \verb|\label{def:pipeline}|
(renamed \texttt{def:pipeline-val} here to avoid a duplicate LaTeX label).
This construction shares its source label with \S\ref{sec:pipelines}'s
admission-stage pipeline (Chapter~\ref{ch:algebra}, which keeps the
original \texttt{def:pipeline} label), but the two formalization receipt
files (\texttt{tools/paper-factory/lean-pilot/formalization\_receipts.jsonl},
\texttt{tools/paper-factory/lean-lake/mathlib\_migration\_receipts.jsonl})
carry only \emph{one} entry apiece under the shared label
\texttt{def:pipeline}, and the Lean sources those entries correspond to
(\texttt{tools/paper-factory/lean-pilot/def\_pipeline.lean},
\texttt{tools/paper-factory/lean-lake/Praxis/Corpus/def\_pipeline.lean})
formalize \S\ref{sec:pipelines}'s admission-stage aggregate-denial
pipeline, not the five-stage validator defined above. So the
\texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified} receipt under this label belongs to
that other construction; this validator pipeline (\texttt{def:pipeline-val})
has \emph{not} been independently machine-checked under either lane, and
its Lean status is reported here as \texttt{not-attempted}, not
\texttt{verified}.


\begin{theorem}[Localization]\label{thm:localize}
Suppose a lawful ledger $\Ledger$ is perturbed to $\Ledger'$ with first
affected record index $j$. The pipeline of Definition~\ref{def:pipeline-val}
reports a Fail whose named record index is $j$, and the stage identifier
names the class of fault; the honest prefix $\fr_1,\dots,\fr_{j-1}$ is not
implicated.
\end{theorem}
Lean status: \texttt{blocked}/\texttt{blocked}.


\begin{definition}[Replay fitness]\label{def:fitness}
Replay fitness is
$\Fitness=1-\frac{\text{tokens forced on unenabled transitions}}{\text{tokens the replay attempted}}\in[0,1]$,
represented as Q16.16 with unit $\code{0x0001\_0000}=65536$; the
\code{token\_replay} stage accepts a record iff its replayed fitness
equals that unit.
\end{definition}
\begin{proposition}[Fitness characterizes conformance]\label{prop:fitness}
A record's replay attains $\Fitness=\code{0x0001\_0000}$ iff its lifecycle
is a genuine firing sequence of the fixed POWL token model; otherwise the
first forced consumption localizes the nonconformant step, and the stage
fails naming that record.
\end{proposition}
Source: \texttt{02\_receipt\_cryptography.tex}; both
\texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}. Per the source's own annotation,
\code{prop:fitness}'s core argument is attributed to the keystone paper's
unit-fitness characterization rather than re-derived here; this chapter
cites it accordingly. \texttt{def:fitness} is the concrete, Q16.16 form of
Chapter~\ref{ch:brce}'s abstract \texttt{def:fit}.

\chapter{Signed Receipts, Content Addressing, and Interoperability}
\label{ch:signed}

\section{Integrity versus authenticity}
\label{sec:signedreceipts}


\begin{definition}[Signed receipt]\label{def:signed}
A signed receipt is the triple
$\code{SignedReceipt}=\langle h_{\mathrm{hex}}, s, k\rangle$ where
$s=\mathrm{Sign}_{sk}(h_{\mathrm{hex}})$ is an Ed25519 signature and $k$
the hex verifying key; it is self-contained since $s$ and $k$ travel with
$h_{\mathrm{hex}}$.
\end{definition}
Source: \texttt{02\_receipt\_cryptography.tex}, realized in
\texttt{crates/chatman-common/src/signed\_receipt.rs}; Lean status
\texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}.


\begin{proposition}[Integrity is not authenticity]\label{prop:intauth}
Integrity (\code{verify\_chain\_hash}) checks $s$ against the embedded
key $k$; authenticity (\code{verify\_chain\_hash\_with\_key}) checks $s$
against an externally pinned key $k^{\star}$. The first is necessary but
not sufficient for the second.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proposition}[Fail closed]\label{prop:failclosed}
When the \code{signed} feature is enabled, a missing or unreadable signing
key is a hard error (\code{SigningFailed}), not a silent skip.
\end{proposition}
Source: \texttt{02\_receipt\_cryptography.tex}; both
\texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}, realized in
\texttt{crates/praxis-core/src/signing.rs}.

\section{Content-addressed storage and interoperability exports}
\label{sec:cas}


\begin{definition}[Content address]\label{def:contentaddr}
The address of a stored object $b$ is
$\code{content\_address}(b)=\chainH(b)$ in hex; two byte-identical objects
share an address, any change yields a different address.
\end{definition}
\begin{proposition}[Content-addressed immutability]\label{prop:cas}
In a content-addressed lake, storing the same receipt twice is idempotent,
and mutating a stored receipt changes its address, so the old address
still resolves to the old bytes: history is immutable by construction.
\end{proposition}
Source: \texttt{02\_receipt\_cryptography.tex}; both
\texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}.


\begin{construction}[OCEL export]\label{con:ocel}
The map $\Omega:\Ledger\to\mathrm{OCEL2.0}$ sends each frame to an OCEL
event with event id \code{instruction\_id}, activity the label of
\code{activity\_idx}, timestamp \code{ts\_ns}, and E2O qualifiers to
\code{object\_ids}.
\end{construction}
\begin{construction}[PROV-O export]\label{con:provo}
Each receipt maps to a PROV-O shape: the admitted observation a
\code{prov:Entity}, the manufacture a \code{prov:Activity} that used it,
the artifact a \code{prov:Entity} generated by the activity, and the
chain link a \code{prov:wasDerivedFrom} edge, SHACL-validated against
\code{sr:SharedReceiptV1}.
\end{construction}
\begin{proposition}[Exports are lossless over committed fields]\label{prop:mapcommit}
$\Omega$ and the PROV-O bridge are lossless over the committed fields:
the terminal $h_n$ is recoverable from the exported log's per-event
fields, so exporting does not weaken the chain guarantee.
\end{proposition}
Source: \texttt{02\_receipt\_cryptography.tex}, realized in
\texttt{crates/praxis-core/src/ocel.rs} and \texttt{ocel\_export.rs}
(feature-gated behind \texttt{law-ocel}); \texttt{con:ocel} and \texttt{con:provo} are both
\texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified}. \texttt{prop:mapcommit} is
\texttt{blocked}/\texttt{blocked} in both lanes -- the losslessness claim
is stated but not machine-checked.

\chapter{The Git-Backed Audit Ledger}
\label{ch:ledger}


\texttt{02\_receipt\_cryptography.tex} states the CAS-lock construction
twice, once as \texttt{def:gitlock} and once, restated in a later chapter,
as \texttt{def:gitlock-op}; the append-log proposition is likewise
duplicated as \texttt{prop:notesledger} and \texttt{prop:notesledger-op}.
Per that source's own flag, these are the same content, not two results;
this chapter keeps one statement of each and is the single citation target
for both original locations.


\begin{construction}[Atomic CAS lock]\label{def:gitlock}
An atomic CAS lock for resource $L$ at repository HEAD OID $H$ is
acquired by \code{git update-ref refs/locks/}$L$ $H$ $\bm 0$, which fails
if \code{refs/locks/}$L$ already exists and succeeds atomically otherwise
via POSIX rename; deletion on drop releases the lock.
\end{construction}
Source: \texttt{02\_receipt\_cryptography.tex}, realized in
\texttt{crates/chatman-common/src/git\_runtime.rs}; Lean status
\texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified} (both instances, \texttt{def:gitlock}
and \texttt{def:gitlock-op}).


\begin{proposition}[Audit ledger]\label{prop:notesledger}
The audit ledger is stored under \code{refs/notes/praxis/audit};
appending entries is a commit transition writing hash-chain receipts as
NDJSON notes, preserving immutability of the execution timeline.
Concurrent appends are serialized by the CAS acquire-fail branch of
Construction~\ref{def:gitlock}, and stale locks are force-released by
comparing the locked OID to current HEAD.
\end{proposition}
Source: \texttt{02\_receipt\_cryptography.tex}; Lean status
\texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified} (both instances,
\texttt{prop:notesledger} and \texttt{prop:notesledger-op}).

\chapter{Scope Theorem: What a Receipt Chain Does Not Establish}
\label{sec:scope}


\begin{theorem}[Scope]\label{thm:scope}
Let a receipt chain $\Ledger$ verify and optionally be authentically
signed. Then $\Ledger$ establishes integrity, attribution, and
conformance-as-checked, and no more: it does not establish obligation
adequacy, world-fitness, or semantic truth.
\end{theorem}
Source: \texttt{02\_receipt\_cryptography.tex}; Lean status
\texttt{blocked}/\texttt{blocked}. Per \texttt{rdf/02\_receipt\_cryptography.ttl}'s
own annotation, three of this theorem's proof steps rest on
Chapter~\ref{ch:algebra}/\ref{sec:chatman-rice} primitives from
\texttt{00\_foundations.tex} -- the obligation battery $G$
(\texttt{def:adm}), $\muop$'s determinism and boundedness
(\texttt{def:mu}/\texttt{prop:mudet}), and the Rice specialization
(\texttt{thm:rice}) -- rather than being proved in this theorem itself;
this paper cites those dependencies rather than re-deriving them.


\begin{corollary}[Scope antibody]\label{cor:antibody-scope}
A claim of the form ``this artifact is good because its receipt
verifies'' is an overclaim: it asserts a virtue Theorem~\ref{thm:scope}
shows is not entailed. The admissible claim is the narrow conjunction of
integrity, attribution, and conformance-as-checked.
\end{corollary}
Source: \texttt{02\_receipt\_cryptography.tex}, \verb|\label{cor:antibody}|
-- the second of the two statements sharing that label
(\S\ref{ch:intro}; the first, \emph{the \BRCE\ antibody corollary}, is
Corollary~\ref{cor:antibody-brce} in \S\ref{sec:conservation-thm}). Lean
status: \texttt{blocked}/\texttt{blocked}. This chapter is the paper's
closing statement on the limits of what a receipt establishes, and is
deliberately the last technical chapter before the worked example.

\chapter{Worked Example: A Contract-Claim Law Object}
\label{ch:example}


This walkthrough is unique to \texttt{00\_foundations.tex} and is
reproduced here as a new narrative over the formal objects already defined
in Chapters~\ref{ch:algebra}--\ref{ch:brce}, not copied from the source's
own prose.


A contract-claim payload enters as a raw observation
$o\in\Obs$ (Axiom~\ref{ax:obs}). \code{law judge} evaluates the obligation
battery of Definition~\ref{def:adm} and finds \code{EvidenceRequired}
unmet: the payload is missing a required attachment. By
Definition~\ref{def:ob}, the missing-evidence obligation contributes a
nonzero lane to the denial word; by Proposition~\ref{prop:bottom}
(Mathlib-verified half), $d_G(o)\ne\Adml$, so $\adm(o)=\Rfsl$, and the
object halts as \code{Andon::Halted\{unmet, refusals, at\}}
(\S\ref{sec:refusaldata}) rather than raising an exception. By
Proposition~\ref{prop:obtotal} and Definition~\ref{def:tax}, the unmet
obligation classifies to a definite category (Prerequisites) via a
wildcard-free match -- the classification is total even though the
resubmission has not yet occurred.


The claim is resubmitted with the missing evidence attached.
\code{law judge} re-evaluates the same obligation battery; this time every
$g_i$ is satisfied, $d_G(o)=\Adml$, and by Theorem~\ref{thm:typestate} the
object's typestate transitions along the judge arrow $j$ of $\Life$ into
$\Val$. Admission (arrow $a$) retracts the validated payload onto $\Adm$
per Proposition~\ref{prop:retract}. Manufacture applies $\muop$
(Definition~\ref{def:mu}); because $\muop$ is deterministic
(Proposition~\ref{prop:mudet}), re-running the same admitted input would
reproduce the same artifact bit-for-bit.


Receipting (arrow $r$) computes the frame of
Definition~\ref{def:frame} and appends it to the chain via
Definition~\ref{def:chain}, yielding $h_+$; because
\code{LawObject::receipt()} consumes its receiver
(Corollary~\ref{cor:subcat}), the object cannot be receipted a second
time. Replay of the resulting record attains fitness
$\Fitness=\code{0x0001\_0000}$ (Definition~\ref{def:fitness}): the
lifecycle is a genuine firing sequence of the fixed POWL token model
(Proposition~\ref{prop:fitness}), so \code{token\_replay} accepts, and by
Definition~\ref{def:pipeline-val} (\S\ref{sec:validatorpipeline}) all five
validator stages report Pass. This is the single-object instance of the
five formal objects the worked example is meant to exhibit: admission
(Definition~\ref{def:adm}), total classification (Proposition~\ref{prop:obtotal}),
typestate (Theorem~\ref{thm:typestate}), the chained receipt
(Definition~\ref{def:receipt}), and unit fitness (Definition~\ref{def:fit}).

\section{Cognitive-load capacity as a motivation for bounded receipts}
\label{sec:cl}


\begin{speculative}[Bounded receipts and working memory]
Human working-memory capacity $\CL$ (commonly cited as $\sim 4$, citing
Miller and Cowan) is offered in \texttt{00\_foundations.tex} as a
motivation for why receipts should be a bounded-codomain interface rather
than a full accounting of the underlying system: a verifier is not
expected to comprehend the whole causal history, only a $\CL$-sized
summary of it.
\end{speculative}
This motivates the $\le\CL$-chunk receipt tuple of Definition~\ref{def:receipt}
and the $O(\CL)$ bound of Corollary~\ref{cor:cost}, but the
Miller/Cowan capacity figure itself is a citation to psychology literature,
not a claim checked against this repository's artifacts; no Lean label is
attached to it.

\section{The BRCE byte: a performance narrative}
\label{sec:brcebyte}


\begin{speculative}[Picosecond-eligible admission]
A standing byte $b\in\{0,1\}^{8}$ with 8 named lanes (admitted, evidenced,
budgeted, authorized, healthy, conformant, receipted, replayable)
supports admission/denial/policy-mask/repair/action-selection as
constant-depth (depth 1--3) Boolean/bitwise operations over a fixed CPU
instruction alphabet $I_8$. \texttt{00\_foundations.tex} itself puts this
in language quoted directly below rather than paraphrased: ``[e]ight bits
can select 255 non-null lawful actions without branching'' (line 406),
and ``[o]n machines whose primitive register operations retire within a
sub-nanosecond cycle budget, the admission predicate is picosecond-eligible''
(line 411).
\end{speculative}
No statement in \texttt{rdf/00\_foundations.ttl} carries a
\texttt{math:label} for this material, despite its reuse of \BRCE\
terminology from Definition~\ref{def:brce}: it is engineering narrative
about instruction-level timing, not a proved theorem, and is quarantined
here rather than promoted to a proposition. Because it is unlabelled
prose rather than a quoted \texttt{math:statement}, the two clauses above
are marked as direct quotations rather than presented as this paper's own
independently-derived exposition.

\section{Maximum Reachable Revenue: an applied aside}
\label{sec:mrr}


\begin{speculative}[Maximum Reachable Revenue]
\begin{definition}[MRR]\label{def:mrr}
Let $A$ be a set of client accounts; for each $a\in A$ let
$\mathrm{lawful\_targets}(a)$ be the evidence-gated target stages and
$\mathrm{realized}(a,s)$ the revenue function under stage $s$; the
Maximum Reachable Revenue is
$\mathrm{MRR}=\max_{\text{plan}}\sum_{a\in A}\mathrm{realized}(a)$.
\end{definition}
\begin{theorem}[Additive separation]\label{thm:mrrsep}
If the accounts in $A$ are independent, then
$\mathrm{MRR}=\sum_{a\in A}\max_{s\in\mathrm{lawful\_targets}(a)}\mathrm{realized}(a,s)$,
reducing the joint plan search from exponential to linear in
$|\mathrm{lawful\_targets}(a)|$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{corollary}[Independence precondition]\label{cor:mrrindep}
\texttt{thm:mrrsep} holds exactly when no obligation in $G_{\mathrm{prop}}$
couples distinct accounts; if such coupling exists, the proposer's
obligation battery must be extended with a \code{BlockingConstraint} on
the shared resource, which by Theorem~\ref{thm:mono} only tightens the
admitted set and preserves the denial algebra.
\end{corollary}
\end{speculative}
Source: \texttt{01\_admission\_algebra.tex}. The additive-separation
arithmetic of \texttt{thm:mrrsep} is \texttt{verified} in the Mathlib lane
but \texttt{unformalized} in the bare-core lane after three attempts (an
\code{omega}/\code{rw} ambiguity the receipt records as unresolved
in-budget); \texttt{cor:mrrindep} is \texttt{verified} in the Mathlib lane
and \texttt{blocked} (not attempted) in the bare-core lane. This paper
reports that arithmetic status factually, but marks the whole business
framing speculative per the outline's own assessment: \texttt{def:mrr}'s
revenue interpretation is a market-sizing application bolted onto the
formal admission algebra of Chapter~\ref{ch:algebra}, not itself a claim
about the mechanism -- it is reported here, quarantined, rather than
mixed into that chapter's technical sections.

\chapter{Conclusion}
\label{ch:conclusion}


This consolidation states one equation (Definition~\ref{def:five}),
one quarantine argument for why admission cannot be semantic
(Theorem~\ref{thm:rice}, Corollary~\ref{cor:noadmit}), one algebra of
refusal built on that quarantine (Chapter~\ref{ch:algebra}), one typestate
category for the lifecycle the algebra gates (Chapter~\ref{ch:lifecycle}),
one manufacturing morphism and its bounded, receipted closure
(Chapter~\ref{ch:brce}), one cryptographic chain construction
(Chapter~\ref{ch:crypto}), and one theorem stating what that chain does
not license claiming (Theorem~\ref{thm:scope}).


Not all of this is machine-verified to the same degree, and this
paper has tried to say exactly which parts are which rather than let the
strongest results lend unearned credibility to the weakest. This paper
declares eighty distinct statements as labelled environments
(\code{axiom}/\code{definition}/\code{proposition}/\code{corollary}/
\code{theorem}/\code{lemma}/\code{construction}/\code{disputed}/
\code{speculative}, each opened with an \code{ax:}, \code{con:},
\code{cor:}, \code{def:}, \code{lem:}, \code{prop:}, or \code{thm:}
prefixed label). Three of those eighty are this paper's own
disambiguating renames of a single shared corpus label rather than
additional statements, disclosed in \S\ref{sec:validatorpipeline} and
\S\ref{ch:intro} (\texttt{cor:antibody-scope}, \texttt{cor:antibody-brce},
\texttt{def:pipeline-val}); a fourth apparent label, the bare
\texttt{cor:antibody}, must also be excluded from any such count -- it
never opens an environment of its own in this paper and appears only
twice, both times as a citation of the external source's original label
inside a \verb|\code{\verb}| span of a ``Source:'' sentence
(\S\ref{sec:conservation-thm} and \S\ref{sec:scope}), so a naive text search for every
\verb|\label{...}| occurrence over-counts it as a distinct statement when
it is not one. That leaves seventy-seven statements. Fifty-seven of them
carry \texttt{verified}/\texttt{verified} Lean status in both lanes,
cross-referencing each remaining label against
\texttt{tools/paper-factory/lean-pilot/formalization\_receipts.jsonl} and
\texttt{tools/paper-factory/lean-lake/mathlib\_migration\_receipts.jsonl}
for a \texttt{verified} status in both files. The other twenty are
asymmetric, disputed, or blocked in at least one lane: \texttt{prop:bottom},
\texttt{thm:mono}, \texttt{cor:galois}, \texttt{thm:total},
\texttt{prop:section}, \texttt{cor:assembled}, \texttt{cor:allstages},
\texttt{prop:fleet}, \texttt{prop:embed}, \texttt{prop:payloadcommit},
\texttt{thm:faithful}, \texttt{cor:cost}, \texttt{thm:conservation},
\texttt{cor:orphan}, \texttt{thm:localize}, \texttt{prop:mapcommit},
\texttt{thm:scope}, \texttt{def:mrr}, \texttt{thm:mrrsep}, and
\texttt{cor:mrrindep}.
A smaller set within that twenty -- Conservation of Consequence
(Theorem~\ref{thm:conservation}), the No-Orphans Corollary
(Corollary~\ref{cor:orphan}), the Localization Theorem
(Theorem~\ref{thm:localize}), the lossless-export proposition
(Proposition~\ref{prop:mapcommit}), the Verification Cost corollary
(Corollary~\ref{cor:cost}), the Scope Theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:scope}),
and both antibody corollaries -- are \texttt{blocked} in both lanes: they
are the source papers' own pen-and-paper arguments, not re-derivations
this consolidation performed or is claiming as newly checked. The Faithful
Chain Theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:faithful}) is stated but excluded from
Lean formalization entirely. And one claim, taxonomy totality
(\S\ref{sec:taxonomy-disputed}), is reported \texttt{verified} in the
bare-core lane and \texttt{unformalized}/contradicted in the Mathlib
lane -- but, as \S\ref{sec:taxonomy-disputed} discloses in full, both
Lean lanes formalize an invented placeholder \code{RefusalScenario} enum
with different variant names rather than the real thirteen-variant enum
in \texttt{crates/praxis-core/src/refusal.rs}, so this disagreement is a
property of two mutually inconsistent placeholder formalizations, not a
demonstrated property of the real taxonomy; this paper presents that
disagreement, and its placeholder-enum origin, rather than resolving or
hiding either.

in a single lane -- rather than against either lane's current invented
placeholder enum -- and re-attempting \texttt{prop:bottom} past its
current Lean~4.31 API blocker on \code{List.mem\_cons\_self} and
\texttt{cor:allstages} past its current \code{funext}/\code{congrFun}
plumbing blocker would move several of the claims in
Chapters~\ref{ch:algebra}
and~\ref{sec:conservation} from ``stated'' to ``machine-checked.'' None
of that work is performed by this paper; it is recorded here as the
concrete, named gap between the two states, not as a promise.
\end{speculative}
